precepts.text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour; the seventh is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: no servile work.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.” The seventh day is not Sunday. And the number seven represents completion, perfection; hold on to that, because it runs through everything that follows.

For those who are new, the Sabbath has rules. Is coming together to congregate enough? No. There are laws that apply to the Sabbath day, and the first is the commandment itself: “Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work.”

So there is no working, no servile work, on the Sabbath. The commandment reaches the whole house: “thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates.”

The pattern is the one God set in Genesis 2: six days of work, and on the seventh he rested. God “blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work.” We keep it holy because he made it holy, and our rest from servile work on that day is a similitude of the true rest still to come, when we reign with Christ.

That takes application; living joyfully is something you have to make happen. This woman, this rib, was made for you: that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
precepts.point: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Just as he had dominion over the other creatures, he had dominion over the woman: he named her. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” A help meet is someone to help him through his daily chores and through living, something to his liking, something for him. God first brought every beast and fowl to Adam, and Adam named them all, because he was over them. Then it says, “but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Nothing yet was just for him.

So “the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam”, took one of his ribs, “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” This is the Most High doing this for his son, and that is a gift. The gift still remains today for every man. That is why we call her your rib: there is a woman made just for you, because it is not good for man to be alone.

Solomon says what to do with that gift: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Living joyfully takes application. It is something you have to make happen.

He goes on: “for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” God made this woman for you. She is the portion you have been given in this life and in all the work you do under the sun, so receive her as the gift she is and live joyfully with her.

precepts.text: For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man. Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. So many people spend their whole lives fighting against their God given purpose, and you wonder why you have all these spirits of depression and anxiety: it is because you are fighting against your God given role. You cannot change it, and when you try to change it, it only brings confusion. The sooner you accept the truth of the matter, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself. Sometimes the help starts to think that she is the purpose; no, you are the help meet for me and my house.
precepts.point: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Just as he had dominion over the other creatures, he had dominion over the woman: he named her. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Just as Adam had dominion over the creatures he named, he named her. So there is no confusion about why the woman was made, Paul says: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” “Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.”

People debate and say we all come from the woman, so how can the man be over her? They do not know the Bible. The woman came from the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. God created the woman for the man, and nobody can create or remake their own purpose in life.

So many people, men and women, spend their lives fighting against their God-given purpose. It is self-sabotage: you will destroy your whole house trying to be something you are not. And you wonder why you are dealing with spirits of depression and anxiety and always on edge: it is because you are fighting against your God-given role. You cannot change it, and trying only brings confusion.

Out of all the beasts of the field there was nothing fit for the man, so God made him a woman, and that woman has a purpose: help meet for her husband. Sometimes the help starts to think she is the purpose, that she is the house. No: you are the help meet for me and my house. The sooner you accept the truth, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself; turmoil comes when you leave that place.

That is where it all went left. Eve knew the rule, but the serpent spoke to what was already within her: “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She wanted the position that was over her. Paul goes back to the beginning for the same reason: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve.” “And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” And Sirach says, “Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” All she had to do was stay in her role and in order.

You might think it too far-fetched that your beloved wife, the mother of your children, the woman who takes care of you, could have the goddamn devil over you while you sleep. But the first woman, the first created by God himself, was susceptible to the devil. You think your wife ain't? That is why the head has to keep reminding them of their place and role in the home.

precepts.text: The Lord God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life and man became a living soul. The breath of life is wisdom; it is what activated us and set us apart from every other nation.
precepts.point: God blessed them with his image and with dominion, but the blessing did not end there.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”. God's image is the greatest image there is, and he mirrored man after himself, then gave him dominion and rulership. “And God blessed them”. But the blessing did not end with his image and dominion. In chapter 2, “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.”

The breath of life is wisdom, and it is what activated us. The word of God has to activate your life. God gave us laws to govern us so that we could be that special people; without them we would be just like every other nation. We are at the lowest state right now because we sinned against God, but we do not want to share power with any nation or be all-inclusive. God wants all or none, and we wait in this state until he puts us back in our rightful place.

Wisdom of Solomon 7 shows what that breath is. Wisdom, “which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit”. That is why we understand the Bible and have a scripture for everything we say. She is “Kind to man, steadfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things”. Free from care means free from the cares of this world. Mark 4 names them: “the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” Wisdom says beware of covetousness, so you do not entertain it.

Then the verse that ties it to Genesis 2: “For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Wisdom flows down from the Almighty and molds you, so if she is influencing you, you are tethered to God. Otherwise something else, covetousness or lust, is influencing you. That breath is what God gave us in Genesis 2, and we let something else draw us away. God gave us everything, and we were led away by women, money, riches and cars, as if the things he created were greater than him.

The power of God is his word. Hebrews 4 says “the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword”, the same words used of wisdom, and it “is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Psalms 19 names the pure influence: “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” “the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” We were once simple; now wisdom makes us wise and we see clearly. In 1 Samuel 10:6 the Spirit of the Lord comes and a man is “turned into another man.”

Much is given, so much is required. Christ asks, “why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” The one who hears and does is like the man who “laid the foundation on a rock”, and that foundation lets you endure tribulation; the one who hears and does not is the house that falls. Learn yourself before chasing deep prophecy: get off the sin first. Wisdom is “the unspotted mirror of the power of God”, and James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” “remaining in herself, she maketh all things new”. Tether yourself to wisdom and she makes you new.

People are watching. A sister came to the truth because she saw the camp in the streets and not one brother tried to talk to her. That is the right example: a people made in God's image, living by the breath he gave, set apart from every other nation.

precepts.text: The Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, thy companion and the wife of thy covenant. God was in the first marriage and is in every marriage. A covenant is a contract of commitment and obligation, not feelings. You understand your phone plan and a sports contract but not this one. Treacherous or not, one flesh is still your companion. She will not be bad forever; hormones change, and you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, drive, and wake-up.
precepts.point: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother and cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh. One flesh means inseparable, but not up your wife's skirt all the time as her best friend: without God there is no wife and no family, so the man's priorities stay in God's order. Marriage began as a divine institution, and what we call marriage today is a human invention.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.

precepts.text: God breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.
precepts.point: 'Replenish' means to fill again, and Adam was told to subdue the earth.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Genesis 1 is an abbreviation, and Genesis 2 explains it, the same way Genesis 10 mentions Babel and Genesis 11 explains why it is called Babel. When Genesis 1:27 says “male and female created he them”, Genesis 2 shows how he did it.

“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground”. The dust of the ground is brown: Adam was a black man, and he wasn't walking around butt naked on earth. “and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life”: when he breathed into him, he put that spirit inside him, the spirit that is his Son from the beginning. “and man became a living soul.” That is how Adam was created.

Then Eve: “And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” Eve was created from Adam, and Adam from the ground.

2 Esdras 3 tells the same story and goes further: God breathed into Adam the breath of life, “and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Adam had access to the spirit realm and could go back and forth. He and his wife were the only flesh that could go there, until he sinned. That is why flesh and blood cannot be up there: flesh and blood has that sinful nature. The man who could walk into paradise wasn't running around butt naked. He was ruling.

precepts.text: That they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord.
precepts.point: The tree of life stood in the midst of the garden.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted”, and Genesis 2:8 says the same thing: “the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” Adam's kingdom ruled the heaven and the earth. The man who could go to paradise, where the Lord is, did not walk around without clothes. Then verse 9: “And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food”. What is that talking about?

Isaiah 61:3: “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord”. The trees of righteousness are Israel: us, in paradise, in our heavenly bodies.

Reading Genesis 2:9 again: the trees pleasant to the sight and good for food are a similitude for Adam's sons in the heavens, the righteous. “the tree of life also in the midst of the garden”: the twelve apostles were up there, the 144 were there, all twelve tribes were there. “and the tree of knowledge of good and evil”: that is Satan. The tree people set up and worship in their houses at Christmas references that tree; Babylon referenced it, and Santa Claus is Satan Claus.

God works hand in hand with the prophets. He has Moses write something hard, and he has the other prophets come and explain what it is talking about. Isaiah explains the trees of Genesis: the planting of the Lord is his people.

precepts.text: Like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season.
precepts.point: The tree of life stood in the midst of the garden.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Psalm 1 was read from the top: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”.

The man who delights in the law is the tree. He is planted by rivers of water and brings forth fruit. That is what the trees of the garden are: the righteous, the planting of the Lord, bringing forth fruit.

Going back to Genesis 2:9 with that in mind, the trees “pleasant to the sight and good for food” are Adam's sons in the heavens. The rivers of water point to the next verse: “And a river went out of Eden to water the garden”. The trees stand by the river, and that is Adam's governance: the righteous planted by the waters of God's wisdom, in the heavens and on the earth.

precepts.text: He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.” The first is Pison, which compasses the land of Havilah, where there is gold; the second is Gihon, compassing the whole land of Ethiopia; the third is Hiddekel, going toward the east of Assyria; and the fourth is Euphrates. The Most High is doing two things here. It is a similitude of the waters above, since he divided the waters below from the waters above. And it goes into rulership: there are trees by those rivers, and that is Adam's governance. It speaks of the heavens, but it came down on the earth too.

Sirach 24 names the same rivers: “He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits. He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest. He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.” These are the four rivers of Genesis, and the water is wisdom and understanding. What went forth through all those rivers was the wisdom of God, going to Adam's sons ruling this earth in righteousness. It starts in the heavens, and it is on the earth too.

“The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.” The first man is Adam, and he did not know wisdom perfectly because he sinned. Wisdom is infinite. “For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.” The great deep is space.

“I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden. I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.” The best garden is paradise. The brook became a river and the river became a sea, and that sea is the sea of glass in heaven.

precepts.text: A pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Wisdom said her river became a sea. Revelation 15:2: “And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over his mark, and over the number of his name, stand on the sea of glass”. We overcame the white man and his lies, and we stand on that clear water. The Lord divided the waters from the waters above, and the waters above are the wisdom in paradise.

Revelation 22 shows the river of Eden in heaven: “And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb. In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.” A river, and the tree of life beside it, just as in the garden.

In Revelation 4, “a door was opened in heaven”, and the voice said, “Come up hither”. John went up into paradise, and that is where those things were shown to him. “And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal”. The sea of glass is the wisdom coming from the throne of God. Esau pictures it as the Bifrost, a bridge leading to paradise.

Psalm 148:4 calls on those waters: “Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens.” Song of Solomon 4 calls it “a well of living waters”. Christ said he is the living water, and told the woman at the well he would give her living water. Those are the waters above the heavens, the springs up there. The river out of Eden is that same water.

precepts.text: The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
After the waters above the heavens, Sirach 19:19: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.” The water that flows out of Eden is wisdom, the knowledge of the commandments, and the one who keeps them eats of the tree of immortality.

Song of Solomon 4 describes the same garden: “A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.” Everybody cannot go there. It has an orchard of pomegranates and pleasant fruits, “A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon. Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.”

That goes back to Genesis, where the Lord made every tree in the garden to grow that was good for food. The living waters feed the garden, and those who do the commandments receive the fruit of the tree of immortality, which Adam had access to before he sinned.

precepts.text: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, as trees which the Lord hath planted.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Balaam, “the man whose eyes are open”, saw the vision of the Almighty and said: “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel! As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river’s side, as the trees of lign aloes which the Lord hath planted, and as cedar trees beside the waters.”

People think these tabernacles are houses. They are our bodies. It is us being that tree by the river, planted by the Lord, beside the living waters. Balaam saw us in our majesty when Christ returns.

“He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters”: the waters are poured out from on high, from the Lord, and we will be swimming in those living waters, the waters from heaven above the firmament, not space. “and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.” The king is Christ, and that is the kingdom of heaven on the earth.

These things were brought out to encourage us. They have been hidden for thousands of years, and understanding them builds up our hope.

precepts.text: Living waters go out from Jerusalem, and the Lord shall be king over all the earth.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And it shall be in that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem”. That is wisdom going forth from Jerusalem. The wisdom comes down from the Father to Christ, it goes to the leaders, and the leaders issue it throughout the earth. “half of them toward the former sea, and half of them toward the hinder sea: in summer and in winter shall it be.” That means all year round. “And the Lord shall be king over all the earth”. Christ is going to be king over all the earth, and Adam is going to be back as king over the earth.

So when Genesis talks about the garden, it is talking about the heavens, but on the earth also God's glory and wisdom went out. That is why it mentions the Tigris and the other rivers. God had leaders, men set up throughout those regions enforcing his laws. His trees were there on the earth too, on earth as it is in heaven. The living waters out of Jerusalem are how it will be again.

Back in Genesis 2:15, “the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.” To dress it and keep it means to rule. Adam ruled the heaven and the earth, and we don't know for how long. He died at 930, but his days only started to be numbered after he sinned. Before that he was immortal, so between Genesis 2 and the temptation in Genesis 3 there could have been hundreds or thousands of years. That is the kingdom of Adam. He had children in the heavens, his firstborn, the twelve tribes, and children on the earth.

precepts.text: Scripture uses trees to represent men.
precepts.point: Some of these trees are literal trees, and some of these trees represent men.

note.label: Genesis 2: Adam, the Chosen of the Most High

precepts.why:
Some of the trees in the garden are literal trees, and some of these trees represent men. The scriptures use trees that way: when Christ touched the blind man’s eyes, “he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.”

Keep that in mind reading “Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it.” Not every tree there is a plant.

precepts.text: The Most High had not caused it to rain upon the earth; a mist watered the whole face of the ground.
precepts.point: Up until this point it had never rained on the earth; a mist went up from the earth and watered the ground. Understand the faith Noah had to have, being told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
When the Most High said “I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights”, it had never rained on the earth. Go back to the beginning: “the Lord God had not caused it to rain upon the earth”. Instead “there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.” That mist is how the ground was watered up until this point.

Understand the faith Noah had to have. He was told to build an ark because it was going to rain, a thing that had never happened. He built it anyway.

precepts.text: The heavens and the earth were finished, and on the seventh day God ended his work and rested; the moon made on the fourth day did not dictate the seventh day Sabbath.
precepts.point: If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.”

The heavens and the earth were finished, moon included, and the Most High still rested on the seventh day. The moon made on the fourth day did not dictate the seventh day Sabbath; the count of seven did, running from the first day.

So the memorial of blowing of trumpets is reckoned by the new moon, but the Sabbath stands on its own seven day rotation, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown, always.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “they are black unto the ground”. God made you black unto the ground. He's telling you that you look like him—dark skin, dark and black like him.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “For wisdom is more moving than any motion”. “For she is the breath of the power of God”. Wisdom is that breath. “and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty”. The word of God is wisdom and a pure influence, supposed to influence you to do right. Why can you be seduced into something else? You might love the world; it has hold of you because the word isn't influencing you.

points: It is not good that man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him. So the woman's original function in marriage was established as a helpmeet. He did not say I will make him a romantic lover, I will make him a baby factory. He said the first thing that a man needs, and why you join a union, is because you want that spiritual biblical helpmeet. There is no other reason prior to that. Later he fleshes it out more, and throughout the scriptures you build upon the role of what a wife is.

So even you women as wives, many of you seek a husband because of monetary reasons, which is not wrong — that is part of the traditional values back then. You got married because there was an opportunity for you. There was no career that you held off marriage till you were thirty years old and had fun in college, and had fun means playing the whore, and then got married. You married because you needed certain things from the man. But the number one thing you should have in your mind as a woman, when you seek to get married according to God, is that it is to be the man's helpmeet. That should be one of your chief desires, and one of your strong desires when you are proving a man.

Because a lot of times we say, oh, you ready to be submissive, sisters? Yeah, I am. You are not. You are thinking about the rod. You are thinking about somebody to watch Netflix with. That is why you start fixing them plates two months in. You are trying to seduce them.

Here is the part where sisters get it twisted, because there are sisters shifting in their seat when I say things like that. It is fine, you can be mad. You are mad with God. It does not mean that women are to be unintelligent. It does not mean that they are voiceless either. It does not mean that they are incapable. Proverbs 31 basically destroys that caricature. So anybody that comes to you and tries to say that when we push biblical marriage we suppress the woman, all you have got to do is give them Proverbs 31. This sounds like a woman that is capable, intelligent, and brings value to the relationship and the family.

You cannot build a family without the woman, and likewise a woman cannot be the dad and everything else. You need both. There is an interdependency. But that virtuous woman is very strong, she is extraordinarily capable, and women should strive to that — not some lazy woman who thinks that because she has the box for her man, that is all she needs to bring to the table. When the honeymoon is over, a man filled with purpose has other things he wants to focus on. Not saying he is going to forget about wanting to have sex — sex nourishes the marriage — but it might slow down and space out. At least a man that is about putting in work, because if you spend all your time chasing box then you are up under her skirt, and God called us for more. That is when he starts to see the issues in the marriage. Her strength operates with order. She has her role, she has her strength, she has her gifts that God gave her to fulfil in the nation and in the marriage, but it has to be with order.
